exposure: neonatal factors (birth weight, gestational age, gender, mode of delivery)
cohort: 1000 neonates born in Maternity and Child Hospital, Government General Hospital, Nellore, India, who were examined within the first week of life, irrespective of gestational age, sex, and mode of delivery.
finding: The study found a high prevalence (89.9%) of neonatal dermatoses, which were significantly associated with both neonatal factors (birth weight, gestational age, gender, mode of delivery) and maternal factors (consanguinity, parity, mother's age).
mod_finding: Sebaceous hyperplasia, Mongolian spot, Physiological desquamation, Milia, Miliaria, and Transient Neonatal Pustular Melanosis were commonly observed in babies born through caesarean section, while Epstein pearl and sacral dimple were common in those born through vaginal delivery.
cross-section timing: within the first week of life
birth_weight: Varied, including low birth weight neonates (as it was a factor studied).
gest_age: Varied, including preterm, term, and post-term babies (as it was a factor studied).
